section_summary: This section follows American and British oil companies’ disputes with Japan over sales quotas, tariffs, and oil stock requirements in 1937. Embassy reports assess Japan’s plan to produce synthetic fuel from coal and its likely effect on foreign companies. Later documents address Japanese fuel policy in 1938 and, in 1939, concern about American neutrality legislation and oil exports.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2233 on foreign oil interests, concluding page
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The despatch closes by weighing the next Japanese cabinet’s significance for oil companies and listing five enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Concludes a despatch on foreign oil companies’ position and lists five enclosures.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Matsushima on petroleum
subfiles.about: Dickover protests cuts to Standard-Vacuum’s Korean quotas and questions whether Japan’s assurances permit further investment.
subfiles.summary: Matsushima says he is pressing the Ministry of Commerce and Industry for an adjustment and explains the intended strength of its written assurances.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Matsushima, Meyer, and Ely
subfiles.about: Company representatives challenge Korean gasoline and Japanese kerosene quota decisions despite government assurances.
subfiles.summary: Matsushima awaits a reply from the overseas authorities. Meyer and Ely provide protests and explain that stock agreements with Mitsui depend on reliable assurances about their future trade.

subfiles.title: Japanese note verbale to the United States Embassy
subfiles.about: Japan confirms four assurances to Standard-Vacuum while urging compliance with petroleum regulations.
subfiles.summary: The government denies intending discrimination or expulsion and says its earlier reply confirmed the company’s four requested points.

subfiles.title: Unofficial Japanese statement on quotas and tariffs
subfiles.about: Japan explains its 1936 kerosene allocations and proposed petroleum tariff treatment.
subfiles.summary: It attributes domestic firms’ higher kerosene quotas to increased home output and argues that proposed customs treatment applies without distinction.

subfiles.title: Japanese note verbale to the British Embassy
subfiles.about: Japan gives Rising Sun Petroleum assurances and answers British concerns about quotas and tariffs.
subfiles.summary: The note denies discriminatory intent, confirms four earlier points, explains kerosene allocations and tariffs, and urges legal compliance.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding despatch No. 2233 to London
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Tokyo’s January 29 despatch and enclosures on the Japanese oil situation.
subfiles.summary: Forwards despatch No. 2233 and its enclosures for the Ambassador’s information.

subfiles.title: File note for despatch No. 2221
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a report on American and British oil interests in December 1936.
subfiles.summary: Points to despatch No. 2221 in file 894.00 P.R./109.

subfiles.title: American and British oil interests in Japan, December 1936
subfiles.about: The extract recounts failed assurances and parallel American and British representations of December 24.
subfiles.summary: It describes growing company distrust of Japanese policy and suggests a naval news report may have obscured the oil representations.

subfiles.title: File note for despatch No. 2257
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a January 1937 report on American oil interests in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Points to despatch No. 2257 in file 894.00 P.R./110.

subfiles.title: American oil interests in Japan, January 1937
subfiles.about: The extract reviews reduced Korean quotas and Japan’s January assurances to the oil companies.
subfiles.summary: The embassies found the general assurances satisfactory, but Japan’s explanations of kerosene quotas and proposed tariffs remained unsatisfactory.

subfiles.title: Division summary of Japan’s search for oil
subfiles.about: The memorandum summarizes Tokyo’s report on the Imperial Fuel Company and synthetic petroleum.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Japan’s fuel plan and expert views on producing gasoline from coal.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2337: Japan’s search for oil
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy analyzes Japan’s proposed seven-year synthetic fuel program.
subfiles.summary: The despatch details planned output, coal supplies, capital costs, subsidies, and projected 1943 gasoline and heavy oil demand. It expects domestic substitutes and refining of imported crude to replace refined gasoline imports. Foreign experts consider commercial coal-based production feasible but estimate a longer timetable and much greater cost. Grew notes serious implications for foreign oil companies.

subfiles.title: Division routing note on despatch No. 2347
subfiles.about: The note directs attention to the despatch’s warning about foreign oil companies’ future.
subfiles.summary: Recommends close reading of the despatch’s concluding assessment.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2347: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports Korean quota disputes and assesses the long-term prospects of foreign oil companies.
subfiles.summary: Standard-Vacuum and Rising Sun face reduced Korean quotas while seeking a response from Japanese authorities. The Embassy declines immediate informal intervention and examines Japan’s synthetic fuel and domestic refining plans. It warns that rising domestic supply could steadily displace foreign gasoline and kerosene imports and urges company headquarters to decide on a long-term policy.

subfiles.title: Joint cabled message from oil company directors
subfiles.from: Directors of Rising Sun Petroleum and Standard-Vacuum Oil, London and New York
subfiles.about: The directors welcome written assurances but protest quota cuts and threatened tariff discrimination.
subfiles.summary: The directors compare their shrinking shares of gasoline and heavy oil trade with 1933 levels. They say administrative practice conflicts with Japan’s assurances and request further written responses on Japanese and Korean quotas and proposed import duties.

subfiles.title: Division summary of despatch No. 2347
subfiles.to: Mr. Sayre and Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The memorandum highlights the Embassy’s warning that synthetic oil may displace foreign companies.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Japan’s fuel plan and the Embassy’s recommendation that foreign companies settle on a policy for their future trade.

subfiles.title: File note for memorandum on Standard-Vacuum claims
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a conversation on Standard-Vacuum’s Manchukuo claims and position in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Points to a memorandum filed under 893.6363 Manchuria/204.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram No. 136 on Korean gasoline quotas
subfiles.about: The Embassy anticipates a request to represent the companies over unresolved Korean quotas.
subfiles.summary: Grew says the Foreign Office expects embassy inquiries and sees no reason to withhold representations under the January assurances.

subfiles.title: Department telegram No. 73 authorizing representations
subfiles.about: The Department authorizes representations about Korean quotas if Britain acts similarly.
subfiles.summary: Leaves the form of representations to the Embassy and asks for a telegraphic report of any action.

subfiles.title: Parker letter on Korean quota negotiations
subfiles.about: Parker reports Foreign Office efforts to permit normal sales while the Korean quota petition is pending.
subfiles.summary: Quotes a Yokohama cable and says the companies await results of a May 6 meeting.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck acknowledgment of Parker’s May 4 letter
subfiles.about: Hornbeck acknowledges Parker’s update on Korean oil quotas.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Parker for keeping the Department informed.

subfiles.title: Parker letter reporting the May 6 meeting
subfiles.about: Parker relays an optimistic Foreign Office report while Korean authorities still refuse continued normal sales.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office links consideration to oil stock arrangements with Mitsui and promises further efforts toward a Korean decision.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck acknowledgment of Parker’s May 11 letter
subfiles.about: Hornbeck acknowledges Parker’s update on the Korean oil situation.
subfiles.summary: Notes the apparently favorable turn and thanks Parker for updates.

subfiles.title: Division memorandum on Parker’s May 24 letter
subfiles.about: The memorandum recommends conditional authorization of embassy representations on Korean quotas.
subfiles.summary: It also addresses Manchurian claims and recommends a telephone discussion with Parker before drafting instructions.

subfiles.title: Parker letter requesting action on Korea
subfiles.about: Parker forwards a cable on Manchukuo compensation and asks for stronger embassy action on exhausted Korean quotas.
subfiles.summary: He reports suspended Korean gasoline sales and requests instructions for representations seeking prompt settlement under Japan’s assurances.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram No. 142 on Japanese quota reply
subfiles.about: Grew reports a fairly satisfactory Japanese reply on Korean quotas.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy and Standard interests agree that authorized representations are unnecessary for now.

subfiles.title: Confidential Hornbeck letter to Parker
subfiles.about: Hornbeck confidentially relays the Embassy’s report of a satisfactory Japanese quota reply.
subfiles.summary: Says embassy representations are presently unnecessary and asks Parker to protect the information’s source.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation with Standard-Vacuum
subfiles.about: Vincent informs Standard-Vacuum that the Embassy has authority to raise Korean quotas.
subfiles.summary: May thanks the Department on Parker’s behalf.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram No. 286 on oil stock obligations
subfiles.about: Grew reports a Japanese Fuel Bureau approach urging foreign companies to settle oil storage obligations.
subfiles.summary: The British Commercial Counselor believes companies should respond; Standard-Vacuum has sought instructions from New York.

subfiles.title: Winterbottom letter forwarding fuel policy report
subfiles.about: Winterbottom forwards information from a Japanese correspondent on Japan’s new fuel policy.
subfiles.summary: Offers the enclosed oil policy report while mentioning interrupted Shanghai radio service.

subfiles.title: Japan’s fuel policy
subfiles.about: The report surveys Japan’s 1938 fuel measures and reproduces proposed oil resource development rules.
subfiles.summary: It describes plans for oil exploration, synthetic fuel, gasoline purchase licenses, and budget support for fuel research and production. It then sets out provisions of the Oil Resources Development Act governing drilling plans, subsidies, state oversight, military orders, inspections, and penalties.

subfiles.title: Welles acknowledgment of fuel policy report
subfiles.about: Welles acknowledges Winterbottom’s letter and enclosed memorandum on Japanese fuel policy.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Winterbottom for sending information of interest to the Department.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese purchases of Netherlands oil
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a report of sharply increased Japanese oil purchases from the Netherlands.
subfiles.summary: Attributes the purchases to building a reserve stock.

subfiles.title: File note on American petroleum in Japan
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a report on Japan’s dependence on imported petroleum.
subfiles.summary: Says domestic production supplied about ten percent of Japan’s needs.

subfiles.title: Division summary of De Friest conversations
subfiles.about: The memorandum summarizes De Friest’s reports of Japanese concern over American neutrality laws and oil credits.
subfiles.summary: It highlights Colonel Hori’s concern about an oil embargo and his conflicting statements on Japanese finances and foreign rights in China.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3671 transmitting De Friest memorandum
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew transmits a memorandum of oil executive A. H. De Friest’s remarks.
subfiles.summary: Draws attention to Japanese interest in American neutrality legislation, export credits, and Colonel Hori’s statements.

subfiles.title: Conversation with A. H. De Friest
subfiles.about: De Friest describes talks with Mitsui and Colonel Hori on oil imports, American neutrality legislation, and possible sanctions.
subfiles.summary: He says Japanese business representatives sought information about neutrality rules and American credits. Hori feared another Panay incident could stop American oil shipments and asked whether California suppliers would observe sanctions. The memorandum continues beyond this section.
